introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examinations. FOOD AND NUTRITION 1, 0540, JUNE 2026, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, duration: one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until you are told to do so; check that the question booklet is headed "ORDINARY LEVEL - 0540 FOOD AND NUTRITION 1". Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. If you change your mind about an answer, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; if you find a question difficult, move on to the next question and come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Le sujet imprime des fautes (« carryout », « Phosphorous », « ones diet », « Quercitin », « Erypsin », « Crest and upright freezer », « kwacoco bible », « Indicator planned ») recopiées telles quelles dans les énoncés et les options ; les numéros 31, 39, 42 et 48 sont imprimés sans point.

Question 44 : la fin de la ligne est coupée au bord de la page (« moist hea... ») ; lecture « moist heat ». L'expression « black spot » est inhabituelle ; la clé D (scalds, lésion par chaleur humide) est la seule cohérente avec « moist heat ».

Clés raisonnées mais discutables, à relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : 5 (chemical energy plutôt que heat energy), 12 (option C, fruits and vegetables ; l'option A cite aussi le miel mais ajoute le lait, qui contient du lactose), 25 (biscuit and yoghurt), 27 (grains and vegetable), 39 (compressor and absorption), 42 (plastic plutôt que wood), 44, 49 (cutlery plutôt que spoons ou knives).

Converties en ouvertes sans lettre visée (aucune clé établie, options ou énoncé défectueux) : 4 (le nombre d'acides aminés usuel, 20, ne figure pas dans les options), 6 (60, 65 et 70 % se trouvent dans les manuels), 15 (aucune option n'est une enzyme), 18 (deux ou trois groupes de poissons selon les manuels), 22 (les quatre facteurs comptent), 36 (« Much smaller » et « Small » décrivent tous deux de petits cristaux), 40 (defrosting et thawing sont synonymes).
Aucun calcul numérique dans ce sujet (la question 47 est un décompte d'atomes : C6(H2O)6 = C6H12O6, vérifié par Python).

Lettre visée conservée dans le corrigé : 1 (B, catering and hotel management ; food processing and baking défendable), 23 (D, lactating ; nursing défendable), 24 (B, 6 mois selon l'OMS ; 4 mois dans certains manuels), 32 (C, personal hygiene ; food hygiene et kitchen hygiene défendables), 34 (D, vomiting ; diarrhoea défendable), 38 (A ; « Indicator planned » est une faute d'impression), 41 (D, bread mixer ; dough hook défendable), 46 (B, fermentation ; leavening défendable).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two careers associated with food and nutrition are:

*Options as printed:* A) Teaching and dress making   B) Catering and hotel management   C) Hotel management and child care   D) Food processing and baking
questions.corrige_markdown:
Catering and hotel management are careers built directly on food preparation, menu planning and service, so they use Food and Nutrition knowledge. Option A mixes teaching with dress making (a clothing skill) and option C pairs hotel management with child care, which is not a food career. Option D (food processing and baking) is also a food-related field, so it can be defended; the pair most usually given in textbooks is catering and hotel management.

**Intended answer: B (Catering and hotel management).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: careers in the food and nutrition field

questions.enonce_markdown: Functions of minerals and vitamins in the body are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamins and mineral salts are needed in small amounts to regulate body processes and to help the chemical (metabolic) reactions of the body take place. They do not supply energy (that is the job of carbohydrates, fats and proteins), they do not insulate organs (fat does) and they do not withdraw heat from the body.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

choix.texte: To withdraw heat from the body

questions.enonce_markdown: Energy is measured in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The energy value of food is measured in kilocalories (kcal) or in kilojoules (kJ). Grams and kilograms measure mass and metres measure length. Only kilocalories is an energy unit in the list.

**Answer: C.**
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown:
How many amino acids are in the body?

*Options as printed:* A) Twenty four   B) Twenty two   C) Twenty three   D) Twenty one
questions.corrige_markdown:
About 20 different amino acids are normally named as the building blocks of the proteins of the body (some of them essential, which must come from food, and the others non-essential, which the body can make). Some books count 21 or 22 because they add rarer amino acids, so the printed number depends on the book and the usual figure, 20, is not among the options.

**Intended answer: no option is established (the usual figure is 20, not offered; 21 and 22 appear in some books).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The energy responsible for all metabolic reactions is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Metabolism is the sum of the chemical reactions in the body's cells. The food we eat stores chemical energy, which is released in the cells and used to drive these reactions (and to make heat, movement and growth possible). So the energy responsible for the metabolic reactions is chemical energy. Heat energy is one product of these reactions, not their source.

**Answer: B.**
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown:
The percentage of water in the body is:

*Options as printed:* A) 65%   B) 60%   C) 80%   D) 70%
questions.corrige_markdown:
Water makes up roughly three fifths to two thirds of an adult's body weight (the figure is lower in older people and in those with more body fat). Textbooks give about 60%, about 65% or about 70%, so three options can be defended; 80% is too high for an adult.

**Intended answer: about 60 to 70% (A, B and D all appear in textbooks; 80% is wrong).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a monosaccharide.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Monosaccharides are single sugars: glucose, fructose and galactose. Maltose (glucose + glucose), lactose (glucose + galactose) and sucrose (glucose + fructose) are disaccharides, made of two single sugars joined together. Fructose, the sugar of fruit, is the only monosaccharide in the list.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The chemical name for vitamin C is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Tocopherol is vitamin E, cholecalciferol is vitamin D3 and thiamin is vitamin B1.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Minerals that controls the amount of water in the body are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sodium and potassium are the electrolytes that regulate the water balance of the body (inside and outside the cells). Calcium and phosphorus build bones and teeth, iron makes haemoglobin, iodine is needed for the thyroid hormone and fluoride protects the teeth.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Examples of food containing unsaturated fatty acids are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Unsaturated fats come mainly from plants (nuts such as almonds, seeds, vegetable oils) and from oily fish. Coconut oil is a plant fat that is rich in saturated fatty acids, so option C is wrong. Biscuits and pastry (made with hard fats), cheese and egg contain mostly saturated fat.

**Answer: A.**
themes: fats and oils in the diet

questions.enonce_markdown: _____ aids the absorption of Phosphorous.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus from the intestine, so that the bones and teeth can harden. Vitamin C helps iron absorption, vitamin B12 is needed for red blood cells and vitamin A for vision and skin.

**Answer: D.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Glucose is a single sugar found in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Glucose is a monosaccharide found free in ripe fruits and in some vegetables (and honey). Milk contains the double sugar lactose (glucose + galactose), not free glucose, so every option that names milk is less exact. The option that names only fruits and vegetables is the best answer.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A disease caused by an eating disorder is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder: the person refuses to eat enough, because of a fear of gaining weight, and becomes dangerously thin. Kwashiorkor and marasmus are protein-energy malnutrition diseases caused by lack of food, and obesity comes from eating too much energy for the body's needs. They are not eating disorders in the strict sense.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of white fish is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
White fish (cod, haddock, whiting, plaice) store their fat in the liver, so the flesh is low in fat. Mackerel, herring and salmon are oily fish, with fat spread through the flesh.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An enzyme that gives onion its colour is:

*Options as printed:* A) Anthocyanin   B) Carotene   C) Xanthophyll   D) Quercitin
questions.corrige_markdown:
None of the four substances is an enzyme: they are plant pigments. The colour of onions comes from pigments of the flavonoid group: anthocyanins give the red or purple colour of red onions, and quercetin (printed "Quercitin") and related flavonols give the yellow and brown colour of onion skins. Carotene and xanthophyll are the yellow-orange carotenoid pigments of carrots and maize. Because the question calls the pigment an enzyme and two options can be defended, no letter is marked.

**Intended answer: a flavonoid pigment (quercetin for yellow-brown onions, anthocyanin for red onions); no option is an enzyme.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: enzymes and food spoilage in the kitchen

questions.enonce_markdown: Citrus fruits are excellent source of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Oranges, lemons, limes and grapefruit are excellent sources of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Calcium comes mainly from milk and fish with bones, vitamin B from cereals, meat and legumes, and vitamin E from vegetable oils.

**Answer: C.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown: Sweet potato is an example of _____ vegetable.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sweet potato is the swollen underground storage part of the plant, so it is a root tuber. Pulses are dried seeds of legumes, a fruit vegetable is something like tomato or okra, and a bulb is a vegetable like onion.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Fish is classified in _____ main groups.

*Options as printed:* A) Five   B) Four   C) Two   D) Three
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fish is usually classified as white fish (low fat, such as cod and haddock) and oily fish (such as herring, mackerel and salmon), that is two groups. Many books add shellfish (crustaceans and molluscs) as a third group, so both "two" and "three" appear in textbooks.

**Intended answer: two (white and oily fish), or three if shellfish is counted as a group; no single letter is established.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Beans, peas, lentils and groundnuts fall under;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Beans, peas, lentils and groundnuts are the seeds of leguminous plants: they are called pulses (the dried seeds) and legumes (the plants that bear them). They are not fruits, tubers or ordinary vegetables, and they are a good source of vegetable protein.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Substance introduced in food for various reasons are called
questions.corrige_markdown:
Food additives is the general name for substances added to food to preserve it, colour it, flavour it, sweeten it, thicken it and so on. Emulsifiers, flavourings and sweeteners are only particular kinds of additive, each with a single purpose.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best source of high biological value protein for vegan is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A vegan eats no animal product. Kidney and butter come from animals, so they are excluded. Of the two plant foods, soya (soya beans and soya products) is the one plant protein that contains all the essential amino acids in good proportion, so it is a high biological value protein. Haricot beans are rich in protein but lack some essential amino acids, so they are of lower biological value on their own.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
_____ is important for proper meal planning

*Options as printed:* A) Nutrient content   B) Age   C) Season   D) Money in hand
questions.corrige_markdown:
A meal plan must give the right nutrients, suit the age and activity of the people who eat it, make use of the foods in season and fit the money available (the family budget). All four options are factors of meal planning, so no letter can be marked as the only correct one.

**Intended answer: all four factors matter in meal planning (nutrient content is the most basic one); no single letter is established.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Another name for a breastfeeding mother is _____ mother

*Options as printed:* A) nursery   B) nursing   C) feeding   D) lactating
questions.corrige_markdown:
A woman who is producing milk to feed her baby is called a lactating mother in Food and Nutrition (lactation = milk production). "Nursing mother" is also commonly used for the same woman, so two options can be defended; "nursery" and "feeding" mother are not standard terms. The technical term is lactating.

**Intended answer: D (lactating).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
When should a baby be introduced to mixed diet.

*Options as printed:* A) 3 months   B) 6 months   C) 4 months   D) 5 months
questions.corrige_markdown:
The World Health Organization advises exclusive breastfeeding for about the first six months, then solid foods (mixed diet) added to breast milk from 6 months. Some textbooks say weaning begins between 4 and 6 months, so 4 months can also be found, but milk alone no longer meets the baby's needs after about 6 months. The intended answer is 6 months.

**Intended answer: B (6 months).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is a convenient food:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convenience foods are foods bought ready to eat or partly prepared, which save time in the kitchen. Biscuits and yoghurt are factory-prepared and can be eaten at once. Fried rice, fish pie, kwacoco bible, ndole and boiled cocoyam are dishes cooked at home, so they are not convenience foods.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first meal of the day is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Breakfast is the first meal of the day, taken in the morning to "break the fast" of the night. Lunch is the midday meal and supper is the last meal of the day.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Half of ones diet should be made up of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Healthy-eating guides advise that about half of the diet should come from plant foods: cereals and other starchy foods (grains) together with vegetables. Fats and sugars should be eaten in small amounts, and milk and cheese form only a smaller share of the plate.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One dietary recommendation is to eat more:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dietary guidelines advise people to eat more vegetables and fruit (fibre, vitamins and minerals) and to cut down on fat, sugar and salt. Options A, B and D recommend foods rich in fat, sugar or energy, which is the opposite of the advice.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Insulin in the body is produced by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Insulin is a hormone made by the pancreas (in the islets of Langerhans). It lowers the level of glucose in the blood. The liver makes bile, which the gall bladder stores, and the small intestine finishes digestion and absorbs food.

**Answer: B.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: The end product of protein digestion is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Proteins are broken down by enzymes (pepsin in the stomach, trypsin and erepsin in the small intestine) into amino acids, which are absorbed into the blood. Pepsin, trypsin and erepsin (printed "Erypsin") are the enzymes that do the digesting, not the end product.

**Answer: C.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown: Bile and pancreatic juice is secreted in the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bile (from the liver, stored in the gall bladder) and pancreatic juice (from the pancreas) both pour into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine, where they act on the food coming from the stomach. The mouth makes saliva and the stomach makes gastric juice.

**Answer: D.**
themes: digestion of food in the human body

questions.enonce_markdown:
Never cough, spit, sneeze over food is a _____ rule.

*Options as printed:* A) food hygiene   B) Food purchase hygiene   C) personal hygiene   D) kitchen hygiene
questions.corrige_markdown:
Personal hygiene rules are the rules a food handler follows about their own body: wash hands, cover hair, never cough, spit or sneeze over food, and so on. "Food hygiene" and "kitchen hygiene" are wider terms for the whole subject or for the cleanliness of the room, and "food purchase hygiene" is about buying food. The most precise answer is personal hygiene.

**Intended answer: C (personal hygiene).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is associated with browning disorder:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Apple is the classic example of enzymic browning: when it is cut or bruised, enzymes in the flesh react with oxygen from the air and the surface turns brown. Citrus fruit contains vitamin C and acid, which prevent browning, and cabbage and cauliflower are not the usual examples of this browning.

**Answer: A.**
themes: enzymes and food spoilage in the kitchen

questions.enonce_markdown:
_____ is an effect of food poisoning caused by staphylococcus.

*Options as printed:* A) Diarrhea   B) Fever   C) Headache   D) Vomiting
questions.corrige_markdown:
Staphylococcal food poisoning starts quickly (a few hours after eating) with sudden nausea and vomiting, then stomach cramps and often some diarrhoea. Fever and headache are not typical. Because diarrhoea can also occur, two options can be defended, but vomiting is the best-known first effect.

**Intended answer: D (Vomiting).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: _____ bacteria require oxygen to grow and multiply.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Aerobic bacteria need oxygen to grow. Anaerobic bacteria grow without oxygen, pathogenic bacteria are those that cause disease, and cocci describes the round shape of some bacteria.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe ice crystal when food is quickly Frozen:

*Options as printed:* A) Large   B) Very large   C) Much smaller   D) Small
questions.corrige_markdown:
In quick freezing the food passes through the freezing point rapidly, so only small ice crystals form. They do little damage to the cells of the food, which keeps its texture and loses little liquid on thawing. In slow freezing large crystals form and burst the cell walls. "Much smaller" and "small" both describe small crystals, so two options can be defended.

**Intended answer: small ice crystals (C "Much smaller" and D "Small" both fit); large crystals belong to slow freezing.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important factor of a well-planned kitchen is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A well-planned kitchen is safe, hygienic and saves time and effort. So it should reduce the risk of accidents. A good plan reduces, not increases, cooking time and effort, and personal hygiene must be encouraged, not avoided.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two parts of a microwave cooker are:

*Options as printed:* A) Indicator planned and cavity   B) Magnetron  and burner   C) Guide and grill   D) Door and oven
questions.corrige_markdown:
A microwave oven has a magnetron (which makes the microwaves), a cooking cavity (the inside), a door, a turntable and a control (indicator) panel. Option A names the cavity and the indicator panel (the printed words "indicator planned" are probably a misprint for "indicator panel"). A burner belongs to a gas cooker, and the oven is the whole appliance, not one of its parts. The intended answer is A.

**Intended answer: A (Indicator planned and cavity).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Two types of a refrigerator are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Refrigerators are classified by the way they produce cold: the compression type (with an electric compressor) and the absorption type (heated by gas, paraffin or electricity). Option B (printed "Crest", for chest) names two types of freezer, and a refrigerator and a freezer are two appliances, not two types of refrigerator.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Allowing ice to get out of frozen food is called:

*Options as printed:* A) Freezing   B) Chilling   C) Defrosting   D) Thawing
questions.corrige_markdown:
Allowing the ice in frozen food to melt so that the food becomes soft again is called thawing, or defrosting. The two words mean the same thing in the kitchen. Freezing is turning the food into ice and chilling is cooling it without freezing.

**Intended answer: thawing or defrosting (C and D are synonyms).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The equipment used in mixing bread is:

*Options as printed:* A) Blender   B) Dough hook   C) Mincer   D) bread mixer
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bread dough is mixed and kneaded in a bread (dough) mixer; the dough hook is the attachment fitted to the mixer to do the kneading. So both B and D can be defended: the machine is the bread mixer and the dough hook is the part that works the dough. A blender is for liquids and a mincer cuts meat. The intended answer is the bread mixer.

**Intended answer: D (bread mixer).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most sanitary cutting board is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A sanitary board must not absorb liquid and must be easy to wash and disinfect. Plastic has a smooth, non-porous surface that can be scrubbed and washed, so it is the most sanitary. Wood and bamboo are porous and can hold germs in cuts and cracks, and a metal surface blunts knives and is not the usual choice.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best place on the body which a home nurse can take pulse is on the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The pulse is taken where an artery lies near the skin and can be pressed against a bone. The usual and easiest place for a home nurse is the wrist (radial artery, below the thumb). The neck (carotid artery) is used in an emergency, but the wrist is the best place in routine home care.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The black spot on the body caused by moist heat is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A scald is an injury caused by moist heat (boiling water, hot liquid or steam). A burn is caused by dry heat (fire, hot metal), a wound is a break in the skin and a sprain is a twisted joint. The printed question is cut at the edge of the page and speaks of a "black spot", but the answer is the injury caused by moist heat: scalds.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mince, meat is described as the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
To mince meat is to cut or grind it into very small pieces (minced meat is used for meat balls, pies and sauces). It is not a paste (mashing), not boiling and not long thin strips.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Boiling of meat until it scatters
Cutting of meat into smaller pieces
Slicing of meat into thin strips

questions.enonce_markdown:
The process that makes a bread dough to rise is:

*Options as printed:* A) Evaporation   B) Fermentation   C) Leavening   D) Kneading
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a yeast dough the yeast ferments the sugar and gives off carbon dioxide gas, which is trapped in the dough and makes it rise: this is fermentation. "Leavening" is the general word for making a dough rise by any raising agent (yeast, baking powder), so it can also be defended. Evaporation is the loss of water and kneading is the working of the dough. The intended answer is fermentation.

**Intended answer: B (Fermentation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The molecular formula for glucose is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Glucose has 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen and 6 oxygen atoms: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}$ (that is $\mathrm{C_6(H_2O)_6}$). $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$ is the formula of sucrose, maltose or lactose (a disaccharide), and the other two formulas do not match any sugar.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of beating fat and sugar together to incorporate air is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Creaming is the beating of fat and sugar together until the mixture is pale and fluffy because air has been trapped in it; it is the first step of many cakes. Folding is gently mixing in flour or whisked egg white with a metal spoon, blending is mixing smoothly and kneading is working a dough with the hands.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Appropriate equipment used on the table to eat are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cutlery is the general name for the knives, forks and spoons used to eat at the table. Spoons and knives are only some of the items of cutlery, and crockery means the plates, cups and bowls that hold the food.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A person who serves food in a restaurant is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A waiter (or waitress) takes orders and serves food and drink to customers in a restaurant. A host or hostess welcomes and seats the guests, and a receptionist deals with visitors at a desk.

**Answer: B.**
